facts.statement: The study is a review that looks at how proteins without standard RNA-binding domains affect RNA processing in ALS.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: ALS is described as a fatal condition involving the gradual loss of motor neurons.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Mutations in genes that do not code for typical RNA-binding proteins are also linked to problems with RNA balance in ALS.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors categorize the non-canonical factors involved in ALS into three distinct functional groups.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: One group consists of regulators of protein stability, whose failure leads to the buildup of clumpy proteins in the cell cytoplasm.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: A second group includes factors that cause RNA toxicity or mess up RNA-protein structures, such as specific repeat expansions in the C9ORF72 and ATXN1 genes.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The third group involves factors that control the movement of RNA granules along the nerve extensions of motor neurons.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: All three groups of factors share a common effect of disrupting how mRNA is processed, stabilized, located, and translated in motor neurons.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The review also discusses how changes in specific chemical marks on RNA, known as m6A and m1A modifications, might play a role in ALS.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue
